newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks slip at open after Dow fall.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks slip at open after Dow fall.

text.p: Australian shares drifted lower from the open on Tuesday after the Dow pulled back and base metals prices softened on the London Metal Exchange on Monday.
At 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 9.9 points at 2,324.2.
The December share price index was 10 points lower at 2,332 and at a 7.8 point premium to the underlying index.

Stocks were lower across the board with selling divided equally between the resource and industrial sectors. BHP was the most active stock in early trade, accounting for about a quarter of the total trading activity.
"It was very quiet yesterday and today looks like being much of the same. Investors are concerned about the possibility of higher rates in the U.S.," a dealer from a Sydney-based brokerage said.

The dealer said the slew of data out in the U.S. later this week was keeping investors on the sidelines and most market talk was centred around the possibility of a significant Dow pullback before the end of the year.
"I expect the market will close about 15 points lower this afternoon," the dealer said.
About a third of stocks traded were steady, while stocks falling outnumbered those rising by a ratio of two to one.
Both the preferred and ordinary stock of media group News Corp opened weaker after the company's ADRs fell in New York on Monday.
